title: High Dispersion Spectrograph for the Subaru Telescope
what_was_studied: Optical design, detector mosaic and first-generation commissioning
numerical_result: HDS provides optical high-resolution spectroscopy with maximum resolving power near 160000
remaining_question: A slit spectrograph needs configuration-specific Doppler validation

title: Nonlinearity in the HDS detector
what_was_studied: Signal-dependent nonlinearity of the two CCD chips
numerical_result: Significant nonlinearity appears above about 10000 electrons and reaches several percent near 50000 electrons
remaining_question: How much does the correction change iodine-region velocities by detector and epoch?

title: Image slicers for Subaru HDS
what_was_studied: Photon collection and resolution using three image slicers
numerical_result: The slicers provide resolving powers near 80000, 110000 and 165000 depending on configuration
remaining_question: Slicer-dependent illumination stability needs separate RV testing

title: HDS iodine-cell observing configuration
what_was_studied: Iodine wavelength reference, throughput and temperature control
numerical_result: The cell covers about 500 to 650 nm and transmits about 85 percent in the visual
remaining_question: The iodine path and unavailable light monitor complicate absolute timing and throughput comparisons

title: HDS current instrument page
what_was_studied: Current capability and July 2026 image-rotator caveat
numerical_result: HDS covers about 300 to 1000 nm at resolving power up to 160000; both image rotators have degraded reflectivity
remaining_question: The effect of the image-rotator degradation on each setup is not quantified on the main page
